page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Telephone tell-tale
title: Telephone tell-tale
description:
Anna gets feedback from Paul today. Following her successful Imperial Lemon presentation, Anna thinks she's going to get some good feedback from the boss.
But rather than being congratulated, she's in trouble because of her poor telephone manner.
However, help is at hand, and from an unexpected person.
This episode focuses on the language used to give feedback.
phrases: I'm a little bit concerned about...

listening_challenge.question: What does Paul tell Anna to be when she is on the phone to clients?
listening_challenge.answer: He says she needs to be more polite.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello. We're back at Tip Top Trading. Anna is very busy dealing with Mr Lime's big order for Imperial Lemons.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes?... Who?... I can't hear you. Mr what? What? Mr Who? I don't know, you tell me. Oh, you are Mr Hu... H-U: Hu. Er... No, Tom's busy. Call back later. Bye. Tom, Mr Hu called you.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Mr Hu-

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mr Hu: H-U

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text:
Anna, Mr Hu is a very important-
Oh! What now?! Yes?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'm going to have to talk to the boss about this.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No. I'm busy, give me your number, I'll call you later. Yep, yep, 6... 8... thanks. Bye! Right, now where was I?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, could I have a word?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Ohhh, he must want to tell me how pleased he is with the Citrus Ventures deal.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Now, Anna... biscuit?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I'm a little bit concerned about something.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: "I'm a little bit concerned..." Doesn't that mean something bad?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes, Anna, Paul is using a polite turn of phrase to say he is unhappy about something. Let's see what he's got to say....

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I think you need to work on your telephone manner.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Work on my telephone manner?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It means the way you talk on the phone is not good enough and you have to improve it – to work on it to make it better.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Perhaps you should think about …

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Perhaps you should think about – that's a polite way of telling you to do something!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, are you listening to me?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, sorry, I was just sort of, err, talking to myself. Could you repeat what you said please?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, I'll start again. I said: I'm a little bit concerned about your telephone manner. You need to work on the way you speak to clients. Perhaps you should think about being a bit more polite to clients; it's important for the image of the company.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh okay.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You can go now – take another biscuit with you – that's my last chocolate wafer, you lucky thing!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anna? Is everything all right?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: What's the matter?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Paul says I need to w-w-w-work on my telephone manner.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well I was a bit concerned about it myself. And I think Tom actually mentioned it to Paul.
But, look, I'll help you if you like. I'm a bit of an expert on the phone. I'll give you some lessons.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh thank you.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Come in early tomorrow morning, before the others get here and we'll practise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you Denise, that's very kind.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Wow! Denise is actually being nice to Anna. Amazing! Although from what I've heard of Denise on the phone, she's only ever gossiping with friends. Let's see if Denise manages to teach Anna anything useful next time. Until then!
